fidelity-joint.headline: Your real risk isn't any single stock — it's that ~76% of this account is ONE bet (AI chips). Exit the speculative satellite (QBTS), trim the expensive half (AMD), keep the cheaper leader (NVDA) — and put every freed dollar somewhere that ISN'T AI.

independentCheck.verdict: Agrees with the direction — disagrees with the reasoning, and the timidity.
independentCheck.gist: A separate reviewer (its own context, its own web research, never saw the desk's logic) called it: the desk was 'trimming the wrong stock for the right reason and holding the right stock for the wrong reason.' Same three actions, sharper logic — cut AMD deeper because it's the expensive, all-time-high half of your AI bet; exit QBTS to your OWN 3% cap, not a soft 5%; and keep NVDA only if you call it a deliberate override, not 'discipline.' Its biggest point, which the cap system is blind to: this isn't a 4-stock portfolio, it's ~1.5 bets.

trueConcentration.note: AMD + NVDA are the same trade (~0.7–0.8 daily correlation, both long AI-data-center capex). QBTS is a higher-beta tail on the same theme. By single-name % you look like 40/36/18/5; by what-moves-together you own ~1.5 independent bets. The 12% single-name cap polices the wrong axis — your risk is almost pure AI-factor risk.

proposals.sizing: Sell ~12 of 15 shares (~$300). Cuts 18% → ~3% (your own satellite cap). Do this FIRST.
proposals.kind: House money + biggest risk cut, cheapest tax
proposals.tradeoff: If D-Wave moons again you miss some of it, that's the cost. But this is the cheapest risk reduction you own: it's already +142%, selling ~$300 takes your original stake plus profit off the table, and your own playbook caps speculative names at 3% — you're holding it at 18%, six times the limit. The one trim worth making even chasing max growth.
proposals.grounded: Revenue last quarter was $2.9M — DOWN 81% year-over-year — against a ~$9B valuation (≈215× sales). The product milestone that would justify the price (100 logical qubits) isn't projected until 2032; today it's an 8-qubit demo. The company funds itself by issuing stock (~27% dilution last year). It's already fallen ~47% from its October high. A 3%-cap science project you're carrying at 18%.
proposals.tax: Realizes ~$176 gain → est. tax ~$44 (assume long-term, ~25% blended). Net cash ~$256. Smallest tax bill for the biggest risk drop — that's why it goes first.

consensus.label: Independent check: agrees, and goes further
consensus.detail: The outside reviewer said trim to 3% or exit entirely — citing your own satellite cap and revenue down 81%. The desk's earlier 5% target was too soft.

proposals.eli5: A risky quantum-computing bet got lucky and ballooned to a big chunk of your account. Risky bets are supposed to be tiny. Take your original money plus the winnings off the table, leave a sliver. Do this one first — safest, cheapest cleanup.

proposals.bull: Quantum is a real frontier; bookings spiked and the cash runway is long. Cutting a 142% winner feels early.
proposals.bear: Revenue is going BACKWARDS (-81% YoY) at 215× sales, funded by serial dilution, with the real catalyst six years out. A meme multiple with no earnings floor.
proposals.risk: Six times the satellite cap. Trim to 3% or exit. Non-negotiable under the playbook.
proposals.pm: Sell ~$300 to ~3%. Take stake + profit; leave a lottery stub if you want exposure. First action of the run.

deployment.headline: Buy what's green on the day NVDA is red. $5,000 into 8 specific names whose cash flows have nothing to do with GPU demand — not index funds, not more chips.
deployment.strategy: Your risk is one factor (AI-compute), not too few tickers. So we buy specific businesses run by different engines: biology (LLY), government budgets (GD), consumer spending (V), insurance + rails + energy (BRK.B), and a real cash floor (SGOV). Concentrated conviction picks, not a closet index fund.
deployment.trap: The obvious 'diversifier' is a trap. Power stocks (Vistra / Constellation / GE Vernova) look non-tech, but on the Jan-2025 DeepSeek AI-spend scare they fell HARDER than NVIDIA itself (VST −28% vs NVDA −17%). They're AI-capex beta in a utility costume. We keep only VST, sized small, and only because it's beaten down ~39% to contracted-cash-flow value — a satellite, not the diversifier it pretends to be.

independentCheck.verdict: Refereed and rebuilt — cut 2 names, added defense, sized the trap small.
independentCheck.gist: An independent strategist (own web research, separate context) proved the power-stock trap with the DeepSeek tape, cut GE Vernova (it IS the AI factor — up 243%, no margin of safety) and Constellation (reactor reconnection slipped to 2031), made the cash floor a real position, and added General Dynamics as the most AI-orthogonal cash flow available. This allocation is its call, not just mine.

deployment.biggestRisk: If the AI-capex boom re-accelerates instead of breaking, this plan underperforms doing nothing — you're buying laggards and ballast while your AMD/NVDA book keeps ripping. That foregone upside IS the cost of insurance. But at 76% one-factor concentration the asymmetry has flipped: you're no longer paid enough for the next dollar of AI risk, and one DeepSeek-grade headline takes the whole book down together.

picks.name: Eli Lilly
picks.thesis: The GLP-1 / obesity-drug juggernaut. Down ~13% YTD on a single pipeline stumble (its oral pill missed estimates after Novo's beat it head-to-head) — but the injectable franchise (Zepbound / Mounjaro) still dominates.
picks.diversifies: Earnings come from prescriptions and biology — zero relationship to GPU capex or hyperscaler spend. A completely different kind of risk.
picks.entry: Good entry — down on a drug-specific miss, not a broken franchise.

picks.name: General Dynamics
picks.thesis: Cleanest defense pure-play: submarines + AUKUS, $130B+ backlog, Q1 EPS beat ~11% with a raised guide. Global defense spend +8% to $2.6T.
picks.diversifies: Revenue is multi-year government appropriations — about as orthogonal to AI-chip demand as a public stock gets. Naval contracts don't care about DeepSeek.
picks.entry: ~5% below its high — quality, not a discount. Reasonable to buy half now, half on a dip toward ~$330.

picks.name: Visa
picks.thesis: The toll booth on global payments. Q2 revenue +17% (fastest since 2022), and it turned the stablecoin threat into a ~$7B settlement tailwind. JPMorgan's top payments pick.
picks.diversifies: Tracks transaction volume and the consumer, not data-center capex cycles. Correlates to the economy, not the GPU.
picks.entry: Near its high (~28×) — a fair-value entry, not a bargain.

picks.name: Vistra
picks.thesis: The ONE re-expressed AI bet: contracted power (20-yr Meta/AWS deals) + nuclear, down ~39% from its high at ~18× forward. You're buying contracted cash flow at a discount, not narrative at a premium.
picks.diversifies: Only PARTIALLY — its cash flows would survive an AI-spending pause, but the stock still carries AI-sentiment beta (that's the trap above). Which is exactly why it's the smallest position.
picks.entry: Best entry on the list — down ~39%, near its 52-week low, with EBITDA guidance reaffirmed.

picks.name: Berkshire Hathaway
picks.thesis: The best shock-absorber you can buy: record ~$397B cash (~59% of assets), insurance + railroad + energy + staples, ~14.6× earnings / 1.45× book.
picks.diversifies: Diversified non-tech cash flows. One asterisk: it recently put ~$21.6B into Alphabet, so a small AI tilt — still the strongest ballast on the list.

picks.name: Johnson & Johnson
picks.thesis: Defensive healthcare: diversified pharma + medtech, AAA balance sheet, 2.3% dividend.
picks.diversifies: Healthcare demand is recession- and tech-cycle-proof — no link to compute spending. A classic low-beta anchor.
picks.entry: Near its high — you pay up modestly for safety. Fine for ballast.

picks.name: 0–3 month T-Bills
picks.kind: Dry powder — fixes your 0% cash floor
picks.thesis: Risk-free ~4% yield, instant liquidity. This fixes your actual structural problem — you currently hold NO cash — and gives you ammo to buy the next DeepSeek-grade dip.
picks.diversifies: Zero equity correlation by definition. The optionality you don't currently have.
picks.entry: Always in season. Buy immediately, no timing risk.

picks.name: Gold
picks.thesis: The one asset that tends to rise WHEN equities panic. Pulled back ~23% from its January top; bank targets still higher.
picks.diversifies: Negative-to-zero correlation with stocks in stress — literally green on the day NVDA is red. Small tail-hedge sizing.
picks.entry: Buying the pullback, not the spike. Fine for a small hedge.
